metadata.note: The Oklahoma City-Ada-Atoka Railway and its predecessor, the Katy's Oklahoma City branch: Oklahoma City (Katy station) - Homa - Marion (Midwest City) - Shawnee - Konawa - Ada - Tupelo - Coalgate - Lehigh - Atoka, 133 mi. Two features sharing one geometry, split at the 1923 change of operator (Rule 4): the Katy (1905 anchor) and the OC-A-A (1923-1944, both ends open). Not drawn: the Katy's Atoka - Coalgate stub before 1904 (no passenger evidence); the Texas and Oklahoma / Missouri, Kansas and Oklahoma construction companies of 1902-04 (no trains under their own names); the Oklahoma City-Shawnee Interurban Co. as a separate feature (never electrified; its track carried OC-A-A trains, drawn here); the Tinker Field spur at Marion and the Lehigh/Coalgate coal spurs (freight only). The parallel former Oklahoma Central (Santa Fe), Lehigh - Ada - Chickasha, is a different railroad and is not part of this layer.
sources: research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt (Feb 1952 Official Guide, OC-A-A table: 'Freight Train Service only')
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing trimmed: drawn from scratch. The OC-A-A's freight years after passenger service ended (sometime 1944-1951), Tupelo - Atoka to its 1956 abandonment, the Santa Fe years from 1964 and the surviving stretch east of Oklahoma City are deliberately not drawn; 1951 is the Guide's 'freight only' listing, not a passenger end year.
not_yet_sourced: ocaa-oklahoma-city-atoka END [OPEN]: 1944 is the last confirmed year and rests on an uncited Wikipedia statistics table (0.2 million revenue passenger-miles). Service ended sometime before Sept 1951 ('Freight Train Service only'). Verify against ICC Statistics of Railways (Class II) or Moody's, which would likely also date the end; Preston George & Sylvan Wood, The Railroads of Oklahoma (R&LHS Bulletin 60, 1943); Corporation Commission discontinuance orders. Fallback if the 1944 figure fails: end 1939 (last dated photo).
ocaa-oklahoma-city-atoka START [OPEN]: 1923 is the takeover year (organized 1 Oct 1923); the first day of OC-A-A operation is not found.

mkt-oklahoma-city-atoka [ANCHOR] 1905 only. Katy service c.1904-1923 is near certain but undated except 1905; Official Guide scans 1910-1922 or Oklahoma newspaper time cards would widen it. The 17 July 1905 Shawnee News-Dispatch time card has not been read directly.

Track dates conflict: Lehigh - Coalgate 1886 (ICC valuation, George) vs 1889 (Wikipedia D&WV); sale of the MK&O to the MK&T 3 Nov 1904 (ICC) vs 30 Jun 1904 (Wikipedia). Santa Fe takeover 1964/1965/1967 conflict is irrelevant to drawn years.

Source conflict recorded: the Oklahoma Historical Society encyclopedia says the OC-A-A operated an 'Oklahoma City-Shawnee Interurban Electric Railway' until 1930; Preston George says the line was never electrified. Not drawn as an interurban.
Homa junction site placed from OpenHistoricalMap, not a source; any Marion/Midwest City relocation for Tinker Field (1941-42) not checked.
avg_speed_kmh (both) and the Katy headway are estimates; the OC-A-A headway is the 1928 count and likely overstates 1930s-40s service.

properties.speed_source: Derived from Preston George's 1928 recollection (about 5 1/2 hours scheduled for 133 mi, about 24 mph / 39 km/h including 10 regular and 12 flag stops); applied to the whole 1923-1944 span, so an estimate for other years (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py over abandoned/disused railway ways, rail-trails and OpenHistoricalMap; shared by both features of this layer.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap with opstrace.py; 133.0 mi drawn (after an 8 m Douglas-Peucker, 135.0 mi raw) against 133 mi documented (Feb 1952 Official Guide 'Total Mileage, 133'; Fowler 133.0; Preston George 'the 133 miles'). Mileposts check: drawn Shawnee 37.2 / Konawa 70.0 / Ada 85.5 / Tupelo 105.4 / Coalgate 119.5 / Lehigh 124.3 against Fowler's 36.9 / 69.4 / 85.1 / 104.4 / 119.2 / 123.8. No OSM way carries an OC-A-A old_railway_operator tag (probed OCAA, OC-A-A, Oklahoma City-Ada; none), so the trace follows the abandoned/disused grade, tagged variously in OSM: 'South Kansas and Oklahoma Railroad' (the Santa Fe-era remnant east of Oklahoma City), 'Atchison, Topeka, and Stanta Fe Railway' (Newalla - Shawnee), 'At and Sf Railway' (Shawnee - Maud, Ada), 'KATY Railroad' (Konawa - Ada) and untagged abandoned ways (Ada - Lehigh, OSM way 224746704; Lehigh - Atoka, way 356603707). STRAIGHT-LINE LEGS (3.6 mi in all, gaps in the OSM grade): east of Midwest City, 97.373 W - 97.326 W, 2.8 mi; 97.293 W - 97.289 W west of Newalla, 0.2 mi; south edge of Ada (96.670 W - 96.660 W), 0.6 mi. Other roads' track used: 0.6 mi of Rock Island-tagged (CRI&P) track - about 0.3 mi near Homa, where the two lines converge, and about 0.3 mi in the Shawnee terminal; 0.1 mi Frisco and 0.1 mi Santa Fe main-line track at the terminals; 1.8 mi of rail-trail (KATY Trail 1.1 mi, on the Katy grade itself; Greenway Trail 0.7 mi near Homa); 0.6 mi of short connectors. TRAP AVOIDED: the parallel former Oklahoma Central (Santa Fe) grade, Ada - Lehigh (OSM way 225103524), was checked and NOT used; every station waypoint Ahloso - Lehigh lies 0.04-0.75 km from the drawn line and 0.8-5.7 km from the Oklahoma Central grade. OKLAHOMA CITY: drawn from the Santa Fe/Katy station area at Reno Ave (start 0.24 km from 200 E. Reno, the station site is approximate) on the Katy approach (ex-Katy track now Union Pacific, and the KATY Trail) east to Homa (about 2.6 mi, matching the report's ~2.5 mi), where the OC-A-A left the Katy; Homa is placed at the end of the OpenHistoricalMap 'Katy 1904-1973' Cushing-line way (35.4695 N, 97.4694 W), not from a source naming the site. Atoka end stops 0.73 km short of the Katy main line (the OSM grade ends there). ALIGNMENT: the drawn line is the last alignment OSM records (as abandoned by the Santa Fe, 1956-1985). Not checked for earlier relocations, in particular any change near Marion/Midwest City for Tinker Field (1941-42); the Katy's pre-1921 junction at Shaw, 1.6 mi west of Homa, is not drawn separately - both eras are drawn on the same Katy approach into the Reno Ave station.

segments.note: Oklahoma City-Ada-Atoka passenger trains, Oklahoma City (Katy station, 200 E. Reno, over Katy track to Homa by trackage rights) - Marion (Midwest City) - Shawnee - Konawa - Ada - Tupelo - Coalgate - Lehigh - Atoka (Katy property, leased). The OC-A-A was organized 1 Oct 1923 to take over the line from the Katy; Homa - Shawnee was owned by the companion Oklahoma City-Shawnee Interurban Co. (never electrified; OC-A-A operated it throughout and acquired it 1 May 1930), and Muskogee Company stock control from 1929 did not change whose trains ran (Preston George). [OPEN] START: 1923 is the first CONFIRMED year (2 passenger engines on the 1923 Corporation Commission roster, Preston George pt. 2) - the takeover year, not a new service: the Katy's trains simply continued, and the exact first day of OC-A-A operation is not known. Confirmed years inside the span: 1923, 1924, 1926, 1927, 1929 (passenger engines/motor cars on the rosters), 1928 (George's own ride: two trains each way daily Oklahoma City - Atoka, about 5 1/2 hours for 133 mi), 1925/1933/1944 (5 / 0.1 / 0.2 million revenue passenger-miles, Wikipedia AT&SF statistics table - uncited), 1936 and 1939 (Condren photos of KO&G/Midland Valley gas-electrics captioned as OC-A-A trains at the Oklahoma City Katy depot). [OPEN] END: 1944 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - it rests on the uncited Wikipedia statistics table (0.2 million passenger-miles in 1944); no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. It stopped before Sept 1951, when the Official Guide prints the OC-A-A as 'Freight Train Service only'. Do not extend without evidence, and do not draw to 1951. If the 1944 figure proves wrong, the fallback is 1923-1939 (last dated OC-A-A train photo, 12 May 1939). Freight continued after passengers stopped: Tupelo - Atoka abandoned 1956, Santa Fe control from 1964/65 (merged 1967), all but a stretch east of Oklahoma City gone by 1985 - context only, not drawn (Rule 1). Headway 720 min is the 1928 two-trains-each-way count; the 1933 and 1944 passenger-mile figures suggest roughly one lightly used train (possibly mixed) each way later, so it overstates the 1930s-40s level.
sources: Segment-level: start year from the 1923 Corporation Commission roster quoted by Preston George, 'Atoka to OKC, Pt 2', The Dispatcher, Mar 1980 (also the 1928 two-a-day count used for headway); end year from the uncited Wikipedia AT&SF revenue passenger-miles table (1944 = 0.2 million) - unverified against ICC statistics; 1936/1939 from Condren photo captions. End date of service NOT sourced.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] 1905 is the only CONFIRMED year of Katy passenger service on its Oklahoma City branch (Oklahoma City - Shawnee - Ada - Coalgate - Lehigh - Atoka). Service certainly ran wider both ways - from about 1904 (line completed to Oklahoma City 1903-04, sold to the MK&T 1904) to 1923, when the Oklahoma City-Ada-Atoka took over - but no other year is dated yet. Do not widen this anchor without evidence, and do not delete it. Evidence: Fowler's Oklahoma station list marks nearly every station on the line (Oklahoma City, Marion, Newalla, Shawnee, Harjo, Maud, Konawa, Ada, Stonewall, Coalgate, Lehigh, Midway, Atoka and others) 'a' = present in the 1905 Katy public timetable; and a July 1905 MK&T time card at Shawnee (Shawnee News-Dispatch, 17 July 1905, p.2) shows one daily passenger train, No. 111, plus a way freight that carried passengers, connecting at Atoka with the Katy Flyer - that page is known only from a search-engine summary and was NOT read directly (verify by hand). Headway 1440 min (one passenger train each way daily) comes from that unverified time-card summary; an undated Pontotoc County history's 'four passenger and four freight trains per day' is not used. The Atoka - Coalgate stub (Katy, 1882/1886) has no pre-1904 passenger evidence and is not drawn separately.
sources: Segment-level: 1905 from Fowler, Oklahoma Railroads passenger stations, table 97 (letter a = 1905 MKT public timetable). The Shawnee News-Dispatch 17 July 1905 time card (source of the headway) was NOT read directly - known only from a search summary; headway therefore not verified.
